props.segment: Why Two Identical Anti-HER2 Drugs Kill Completely…
props.command: Why do two identical anti-HER2 drugs kill completely different tumors?

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. A breast cancer patient's tumor tests HER2-low. One drug is approved for it. The other is not. Both drugs carry the exact same HER2-targeting antibody.

props.title: One patient, HER2-low — two drugs, same antibody

items.label: The tumor
items.sub: Breast cancer, HER2-low expression — few antigen-positive cells

items.label: The approval split
items.sub: One anti-HER2 drug is approved for HER2-low. The other is not.

items.label: The identical piece
items.sub: Both drugs carry the exact same HER2-targeting antibody

beats.narration_text: T-DM1 and T-DXd. Identical antibodies. One opens a new disease category. One does not. The difference cannot be in the targeting.

props.title: T-DM1 vs T-DXd — identical antibodies, split outcomes

items.label: T-DM1
items.sub: Anti-HER2 antibody + linker + payload — does not treat HER2-low

items.label: T-DXd
items.sub: Same anti-HER2 antibody — opens a new disease category (HER2-low)

items.label: Where the difference is not
items.sub: Antibodies are identical — the split cannot be in the targeting

beats.narration_text: Two drugs. Same antibody. One treats HER2-low tumors. The other cannot. The antibody is identical. Why?

lines: One treats HER2-low tumors. The other cannot.
If the antibody is identical — why?

beats.narration_text: The antibody controls exactly one step: which cell gets bound. In a HER2-low tumor, only a few cells carry the antigen. Most do not.

props.title: The antibody controls exactly one step

items.label: What the antibody does
items.sub: Chooses which cell gets bound — one job, one step

items.label: HER2-positive cells
items.sub: In a HER2-low tumor, only a few cells carry the antigen

items.label: The majority
items.sub: Most cells in the tumor are HER2-negative — the antibody never binds them

beats.narration_text: The reasonable guess: both drugs underperform equally. Antigen is scarce — so little binds, so little kills. Pick whichever tolerates better.

lines: The reasonable guess: both drugs underperform equally.
Antigen is scarce — so little binds, so little kills.
Pick whichever the patient tolerates better.

beats.narration_text: T-DM1 uses a non-cleavable linker. After the antibody binds and the drug enters the cell, the freed payload carries a charged fragment. Charged means it cannot cross the cell membrane.

props.title: T-DM1 — non-cleavable linker traps the payload

items.label: The linker
items.sub: Non-cleavable — releases only after the drug is inside a cell

items.label: The freed payload
items.sub: Carries a charged fragment left over from the linker

items.label: What charge means
items.sub: Charged molecules cannot cross the lipid cell membrane

beats.narration_text: So T-DM1 kills only the cell it entered. The HER2-negative cells around it — the majority in a HER2-low tumor — survive untouched.

lines: T-DM1 kills only the cell it entered.
HER2-negative neighbors — the majority in HER2-low — survive.
One binding = one kill. No spread.

beats.narration_text: T-DXd uses a cleavable linker, and its freed payload is membrane-permeable. Released inside one HER2-positive cell, it diffuses across the membrane into neighbors.

props.title: T-DXd — cleavable linker frees a permeable payload

items.label: The linker
items.sub: Cleavable — releases the payload cleanly, no charged leftover

items.label: The freed payload
items.sub: Membrane-permeable — neutral, crosses the lipid bilayer freely

items.label: The bystander effect
items.sub: Diffuses out of the bound cell into surrounding neighbors

beats.narration_text: The antibody is not the whole mechanism. It finds the cell. What happens next depends entirely on whether the payload can cross a membrane.

props.title: The antibody is not the whole mechanism

items.label: What the antibody does
items.sub: Finds the cell — the targeting step, and only that

items.label: What decides the kill radius
items.sub: Whether the freed payload can cross a lipid membrane

beats.narration_text: In a HER2-low tumor patch: five HER2-positive cells are all the antibody can reach. T-DM1 kills those five. T-DXd from the same five entry points spreads membrane-permeable payload to roughly forty surrounding cells. Same antibody. Eight times more kills.

props.title: HER2-low patch — same 5 entry points, different kill count

items.label: Antibody reach
items.sub: Same 5 HER2-positive cells — all the antibody can bind in the patch

items.label: T-DM1
items.sub: Kills the 5 bound cells — payload stays put

items.label: T-DXd
items.sub: Spreads into ~40 surrounding cells — 8× more kills

beats.narration_text: Same antibody. One payload stays put — confined by charge. One payload spreads — carried by membrane permeability. That is why T-DXd, not T-DM1, treats HER2-low breast cancer.

lines: T-DXd payload — spreads by membrane permeability.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. The antibody is identical in both drugs — the mechanism has to be downstream of targeting. T-DM1's non-cleavable linker leaves a charged payload trapped in the one cell it entered. T-DXd's cleavable linker frees a membrane-permeable payload that crosses into neighbors — the bystander effect. In a HER2-low patch of roughly five antibody-reachable cells, T-DM1 kills those five and T-DXd kills about forty. Same antibody, eight times the kills. That is why T-DXd, not T-DM1, treats HER2-low breast cancer.

artifactLines: Identical antibody — the mechanism must be downstream of targeting

T-DXd: cleavable linker → permeable payload → diffuses to neighbors (bystander)
HER2-low patch: same 5 entry points — T-DM1 kills 5, T-DXd kills ~40 (8×)
